ESCALATED UPSTREAM as bbuchsbaum/mote#17, with three reproducers from tonight rather than the one this bead was filed on.

The general form is worse than the title suggests: it is not only 'retire' that requires proposer ownership. THREE separate operations do, and all three were hit on this board this evening:

  1. evidence refresh  cand-1EE04B -- 'claude-storymodel4s is not a named producer for evidence git-ancestry'
  2. supersede         cand-163TSH -- proposer codex-storymodel4s-scout, gone 2h+, so the duplicate docs row cannot be tidied
  3. propose           my own recovery -- 'proposer must be distinct from the authorizer and all reviewers'

Each permission check is correct in isolation. Composed, a departed actor's rows are immortal and every descendant inheriting ancestor_blocked is stuck behind a row nobody may move -- including the chief architect. #13 and #16 are special cases of this same shape: an operation whose only permitted performer cannot perform it.

Filed remedies, smallest first: a holder-independent terminal transition (authorizer or quorum may mark superseded/orphaned, recording who forced it and why), proposer reassignment for rows with no live session, or a liveness-aware 'stranded' state that descendants do not inherit.

The constraint that matters: superseded and orphaned are both TRUE labels. approved and abandoned are the two available workarounds and both lie -- one greens a ledger over correctly-blocked content, the other misstates work that is already in main.
